connections.why: Electron arrangement determines how atoms bond
The type of bonding gives rise to ionic, covalent and metallic structures
Nanoparticle properties arise from their structure and huge surface area
The Periodic Table is organised by atomic number and electron configuration
Knowing how atoms combine lets you write correct chemical formulae
Balanced equations are the basis for mole and mass calculations
Group trends explain the reactivity of metals
Tests for ions build on the reactions of acids, bases and salts
Salt preparations are described by neutralisation equations
Reactivity drives the redox reactions involved in rusting and corrosion
Electrolysis is used to extract the most reactive metals
Electrolysis is an applied redox process at the electrodes
Equilibrium is reached when forward and reverse reaction rates are equal
Titration and yield calculations extend the mole concept
Titrations quantify acid-base reactions to find concentrations
Covalent bonding underpins the structures of organic molecules
Activation energy on energy profiles links to reaction rate
Tests for gases rely on their characteristic chemical reactions
A sound plan must be followed by careful, safe practical technique
Reliable measurements are needed before data can be processed
Processed data supports valid, evaluated conclusions
Rate experiments are a core context for planning investigations
Salt preparation and titration are key prescribed practical techniques
